messages:
Priya - CSM: Heads up — customer MediTech (Dedicated, VPC) started seeing SSO failures after they changed k8s ingress annotations. Calls to Redwood return 401s, runtime logs show auth header missing.

Sam - Support: Ugh. Can you paste repro steps and any raw headers you captured? Do we see this only through ALB -> Istio path? :eyes:

Priya - CSM: Repro steps below (from customer):
1) Hit app via ALB -> NLB -> Istio-ingressgateway -> sidecar -> service
2) Browser sends cookie SSO, ALB rewrites to signed cookie, upstream call to /api/v1/predict returns 401

curl -v '
  -H "Cookie: SSO_AUTH=eyJhb..." 
  -H "Host: api.meditech.internal" 
  https://dedicated.meditech.example/api/v1/predict

Response: 401 Unauthorized
Upstream captured headers (from customer tcpdump):
  :method: GET
  :path: /api/v1/predict
  x-forwarded-for: 10.2.3.4
  x-forwarded-proto: https
  cookie: SSO_AUTH=eyJ...
  authorization:  <MISSING>

Sam - Support: Interesting that Authorization is missing instead of being malformed. Did they have any ingress annotation that strips headers? e.g., nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-set-headers or aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol?

Liam - Eng-Infra: Quick checks: is the ALB doing TLS termination and then re-signing cookies? ALB/NLB sometimes normalize or drop Authorization if using proxy-protocol + TLS at LB level. Also Istio's ext_authz or an Envoy filter can drop headers if configured to sanitize.

Liam - Eng-Infra: Can you ask them to run a minimal curl that shows request line to the ingressgateway directly (skip ALB) and to capture envoy admin listener config? e.g.:

kubectl -n istio-system exec -it deploy/istio-ingressgateway -- curl -sS localhost:15000/listeners | jq .

Also tcpdump on ingressgateway pod: sudo tcpdump -A -s 0 -i any port 443 then grep for "Authorization"

Priya - CSM: Customer tried bypassing ALB and hit ingressgateway directly and saw Authorization present on that request, but when routed through ALB -> NLB the header disappears. They shared ALB annotations:
  alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-type: oidc
  alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/modify-request-headers: "true"

They also set: alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/target-protocol: HTTP

Ingrid - Eng-Platform: That target-protocol=HTTP is a red flag — ALB will terminate TLS and send plain HTTP to nodes; some L7 proxies or sidecars treat that as external and sanitize certain sensitive headers. If ALB is also doing OIDC, it may be rewriting cookie -> Authorization at the ALB level and then not forwarding the header to the backend.

Ingrid - Eng-Platform: Two paths to fix:
- Preferred: Configure ALB to forward the Authorization header (ensure "preserveHostHeader" and any header forwarding settings are enabled), change target-protocol to HTTPS between ALB and ingress if possible.
- Workaround: Have ALB set a signed assertion header (e.g., X-ALB-ASSERTION) and add a safe passthrough rule in Istio to map that to Authorization before ext_authz runs.

Liam - Eng-Infra: On the Istio/Envoy side, check for these filters/settings that commonly drop headers:
- external authorization filter (envoy.ext_authz) with `include_request_headers_in_check` false
- header sanitization via `remove_request_headers` or `sanitize_set`
- `forward_client_cert_details` when set to SANITIZE it can drop or replace client cert headers

Sample envoy ext_authz snippet that can cause drop if misconfigured:

  http_filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.ext_authz
    typed_config:
      "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.ext_authz.v3.ExtAuthz
      failure_mode_allow: false
      include_request_headers_in_check: true

If include_request_headers_in_check is false, some builds strip sensitive headers before the ext_authz check.

Sam - Support: Can we also confirm there's no haproxy/nginx sidecar on the host rewriting/removing Authorization for internal calls? I've seen proxies do that when they think it's a browser cookie auth flow.

Priya - CSM: Customer confirmed no nginx sidecar. They do have a small lua auth filter on ALB target group, not on nodes.

Liam - Eng-Infra: Actionable ask to customer: capture full HTTP trace at ALB (enable access logs), and show request/response header set before hitting nodes. If ALB shows Authorization present and it's missing at ingressgateway, then the issue is on the node path (NLB / proxy-protocol). If ALB already stripped it, then ALB config needs change.

Priya - CSM: Customer sent ALB access log excerpt — shows Authorization present when ALB forwards to target. So the header disappears between node and istio ingress.

Liam - Eng-Infra: That tells us to inspect kube-proxy / host network / iptables or the NLB path. NLB with proxy-protocol v2 can mangle or cause Envoy to reparse and drop headers if connection upgrades happen. Also verify that the istio-ingressgateway listener is on 443 and not re-terminating proxy protocol unexpectedly.

Sam - Support: Quick workaround we can offer to customer: configure ALB to inject an assertion header (X-RW-ASSERTION) with the user's sub and have a small HTTP filter in istio that maps X-RW-ASSERTION -> Authorization: Bearer <token> just for this customer until we patch infra. Note: this is a security-sensitive temporary change.

Ingrid - Eng-Platform: I'll add a permissive mapping in our dedicated gateway config for that customer only (annotation-based) and set a 72h TTL, plus audit log entries. We'll need a change request in infra to make it official.

Oncall: Opening internal ticket: INF-4821 (P1) — "Ingress path drops Authorization header for MediTech dedicated VPC when routed via ALB+NLB". Assigning to Liam. ETA initial triage 2h.

deploy-bot: Created INF-4821 and linked support ticket SUP-9042.

Sam - Support: I'll reply to the customer with the temporary workaround (X-RW-ASSERTION map) and ask for a small maintenance window to apply the change. Also requested tcpdump from ingress node for the time window when they repro.

Priya - CSM: Customer accepted workaround and scheduled 30m window. They provided missing tcpdump from the node; Liam to triage.

Liam - Eng-Infra: Taking it. First hypothesis: proxy-protocol + Istio listener mismatch. Will run packet capture and verify whether proxy protocol header is being processed and if Envoy is interpreting payload as headers incorrectly.

Sam - Support: Thanks team. Please keep thread updated. I'll mark SUP-9042 as escalated to eng and ping if we need legal/infosec review for temporary header mapping. :thumbsup:

Oncall: Noted. If we need immediate rollback we can remove the mapping. Keep logs and tracer spans for RCA.

(End of thread)
